question.text: Which of the following is a key advantage of the trail commission model over the upfront commission model for mutual fund distribution?

answer.text: Trail commission provides a larger one-time payout to the distributor
Trail commission is paid directly by the investor, ensuring full transparency
Trail commission aligns the distributor's interest with the investor's by incentivizing long-term asset retention
Trail commission eliminates the need for EUIN disclosure on transaction forms

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.123-p.124), the SEBI/AMFI framework uses a full-trail commission model. Trail commission is calculated on the net assets attributable to the units sold by the distributor and is payable for as long as the investor's money remains held in the scheme. As NAV/AUM rise, the trail amount rises too, so the distributor benefits when the investor stays invested and the portfolio grows. The Trap: Option A describes upfront commission, not trail. Option B is wrong — trail commission is paid from the scheme's TER, not directly by the investor. Option D is incorrect — EUIN disclosure is mandatory regardless of the commission model. Note: Per p.127, the trail model encourages ongoing service and retention because distributors benefit from a loyal investor base and portfolio growth. Churning — generating fresh commissions through unnecessary switches — is treated as a malpractice in the source (p.305).
